Oruro is the capital of Oruro Department. Its name comes from the ancestral name of the Uru Uru tribe. The city was founded in 1606 as a silver-mining center in the Uru region. After its silver deposits were exhausted, the city was largely forgotten, only to revive in the late 19th century as a center of tin mining. For a time, tin from the La-Salvador deposit was among the world's most important sources of the metal. When tin reserves ran out, Oruro once again fell into decline.

The city's otherwise sleepy pace comes alive during its carnival, regarded as one of South America's most distinctive folk celebrations. The event attracts visitors from around the world. Oruro also has its own symphony orchestra, several churches dating to the 18th and 19th centuries, and the seat of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Oruro.

Oruro is considered Bolivia's folklore capital. It hosts the country's largest carnival, which was included on UNESCO's list in 2001. The celebration preserves elements of the region's Indigenous pre-Columbian religious traditions.

## Isla de la Juventud — a lively island for young travelers!

Isla de la Juventud is known in Cuba as a popular holiday destination for young people. Young visitors from all over the world come here to have fun and enjoy themselves. They arrive in groups, as couples, or on their own, hoping to meet new people.

## Isla de la Juventud — a paradise for divers!

The island is also a paradise for divers and adventure seekers. Its scenery is beautiful, with mysterious sheer cliffs, steep underwater drop-offs, and exceptionally rich marine life.

## Isla de la Juventud — an island for every traveler!

Isla de la Juventud is Cuba's second-largest island and belongs to the Los Canarreos Archipelago. Hundreds of years ago, it served as a refuge for pirates. That history, together with the remarkable beauty of the seabed, makes the island so attractive to divers. Its most popular diving area is Punta Frances Marine National Park, which has 56 dive sites. The island's beaches, framed by green hills and citrus groves, offer spectacular views of the Caribbean Sea. Near its capital, the historic town of Nueva Gerona, stands Presidio Modelo prison, where Fidel Castro was held; a museum now operates on its grounds. Another important attraction is the Cueva Punta del Este cave system, where more than 230 pictographs dating to 800 BC have been found. To learn more about the island's natural diversity, visit the Jungla de Jones and Los Indios nature reserves.

### Margarita Island — the pearl of Venezuela!

Margarita is a beautiful island located just off Venezuela's coast. It was discovered by Christopher Columbus. The abundance of pearl oysters in its coastal waters encouraged rapid colonization and gave the island its name, Margarita, meaning "pearl."

Today, the island has become a jewel of tourism. Porlamar is Margarita's capital and a well-known duty-free shopping destination.

## A wonderful holiday on Margarita Island

### Margarita Island — a jewel of tourism!

First-class hotels in the city provide places for visitors to relax and enjoy themselves. Among the beautiful historic landmarks are Fort La Caranta, Fort España, and Castillo de San Carlos in Pampatar. The hot springs around the town of Río Caribe add their own charm and invite visitors to bathe. Magnificent palm-fringed beaches and surfing spots are scattered across the island. Restaurants and entertainment venues line the coast, and the hours seem to fly by. It is the kind of place you want to return to again and again.

## Ometepe — Nicaragua's volcanic island

### Ometepe Island — "the place of two hills"!

The name Ometepe translates as "place of two hills." The island is volcanic in origin, and those two hills are, in fact, two active volcanoes. The island is situated in Lake Nicaragua.

## Visit Ometepe Island for unforgettable experiences!

Magnificent views, spectacular nature, abundant fruit, a peaceful atmosphere, and, of course, the chance to climb a volcano are what bring travelers from around the world to Ometepe. Its landscape is dominated by two majestic volcanoes, Concepción and Maderas, which are also major attractions. Climbing to the summit of Maderas rewards you with breathtaking views, and you can bathe in a lagoon whose waters are believed to have beneficial effects on the body. Ometepe is protected as a biosphere reserve for its exceptional natural environment, flora, and fauna.
